query: Earlier studies of conventional metallic multilayers provide a general framework for deformation, but its conclusions may not transfer directly to high-entropy-alloy systems because compositional complexity, severe lattice distortion, and short-range order are associated with unusual deformation behavior. Preliminary evidence from FCC/BCC high-entropy-alloy multilayers remains insufficient to establish what controls creep or when a given response dominates. Within the constraints of retaining a nanoscale multilayer coating and balancing strength with deformation tolerance, what testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain progressive plastic deformation under sustained loading? State what governs the behavior and why, an unspecified controlled comparison that would expose it, predicted observations relative to the starting baseline, boundary conditions, relevant prior support, and a result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Severe lattice distortion in high-entropy-alloy multilayers governs progressive plastic deformation under sustained loading.
generation.conditions: Retention of nanoscale multilayer coating, balanced strength with deformation tolerance
generation.mechanism: Lattice distortion leads to unusual deformation behavior, controlling creep and dominating the response
generation.predicted_outcome: Increased plastic deformation with increased lattice distortion
generation.baseline: Low lattice distortion, minimal plastic deformation
generation.boundary: Nanoscale multilayer coating retention, balanced strength and deformation tolerance
generation.uncertainty: Insufficient evidence to establish what controls creep or when a given response dominates

falsification_experiment.design: Controlled comparison of high-entropy-alloy multilayers with varying lattice distortion
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If no correlation between lattice distortion and plastic deformation is observed, the hypothesis is falsified
